title: Virginia Beach Strong Act
official_summary:
Virginia Beach Strong Act

This bill confirms that cash contributions made on or after May 31, 2019, for the exclusive benefit of the families of the dead or wounded victims of the mass shooting in Virginia Beach, Virginia on May 31, 2019, shall be treated as tax deductible contributions.

The bill also confirms that payments made on or after May 31, 2019, and on or before June 1, 2021, to the spouse or any dependent of the dead or wounded victims of such mass shooting by an tax-exempt organizations shall be treated as related to such organization's tax-exempt purpose and shall not be treated as inuring to the benefit of any private individual, if such payments are made in good faith using a reasonable and objective formula that is consistently applied with respect to such victims.

summary.headline: A 2019 law confirms that certain donations and payments made for the families of the Virginia Beach shooting victims get specific tax treatment.
summary.what_it_does: The law says cash gifts made on or after May 31, 2019, for the families of people killed or wounded in the Virginia Beach mass shooting count as tax-deductible contributions. It also says that certain payments by tax-exempt organizations to the spouses or dependents of those victims, made from May 31, 2019 through June 1, 2021, count as related to the organization's tax-exempt purpose. This applies only if the payments were made in good faith, used a reasonable and objective formula, and were applied consistently to the victims.

who_it_affects.group: Families of people killed or wounded in the May 31, 2019 Virginia Beach mass shooting
who_it_affects.how: Their spouses and dependents may receive cash support from donors and tax-exempt organizations that the law treats as tax-favored.

who_it_affects.group: People who gave cash to help the families of the Virginia Beach shooting victims
who_it_affects.how: Cash gifts made on or after May 31, 2019, for those families are treated as tax-deductible contributions.

who_it_affects.group: Tax-exempt organizations that paid victims' spouses or dependents
who_it_affects.how: Qualifying payments made from May 31, 2019 through June 1, 2021, are treated as related to their tax-exempt purpose rather than as benefits to private individuals.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law December 20, 2019, with the tax treatment applying retroactively to gifts and payments made starting May 31, 2019; the organization payment rule covers payments made through June 1, 2021.
